verdict: Reported revenue fell 25% on license timing and the sale of Kepware and ThingWorx, even as recurring contracts (ARR, excluding the sold businesses) grew 8% — and PTC agreed to be acquired by Schneider Electric, so it stopped giving guidance.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: -25% YoY, hit by license timing under ASC 606

kpis.label: ARR excl. divested businesses
kpis.note: +8% YoY — the annualized value of active subscription contracts

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: Down from $100M, after about $75M of divestiture-related cash taxes and $24M of divestiture costs

segments.name: License
segments.note: The license part of subscription software sales — lumpy, because much of it is booked up front when a contract starts

segments.name: Support and cloud services
segments.note: Support, hosting and cloud services for its industrial software — the steady, recurring part

segments.name: Professional services
segments.note: Consulting and help getting the software installed and used

opex.name: Amortization of acquired intangibles
opex.note: Spreading the cost of software and other assets bought in acquisitions

takeaways.title: Headline revenue fell sharply
takeaways.text: Revenue was $673M, down from $894M a year ago. License revenue fell 45% on contract timing, while support and cloud revenue was almost flat at $382M.

takeaways.title: The contract base still grew
takeaways.text: ARR excluding the divested Kepware and ThingWorx businesses rose 8% to $2,508M, showing the underlying subscription book kept growing.

takeaways.title: Profit halved, and a takeover is pending
takeaways.text: GAAP EPS was $1.44 versus $2.88 a year ago. On October 5, 2026 PTC agreed to be acquired by Schneider Electric and suspended guidance and earnings calls.

oneTimers: Impairment and other charges of $6M in the quarter
About $75M of divestiture-related cash taxes and $24M of divestiture-related costs weighed on Q4 cash flow (not on GAAP profit the same way)
footerNote: Amounts in the release are in thousands and are rounded here to whole $M; segment lines are the release's supplemental split of revenue into license, support and cloud services, and professional services, which sums to total revenue. PTC's fiscal year ends September 30, so this is its fiscal Q4.
